regionBrowser.suggested: Before a row of quick picks: the region of the photo or page, and the regions picked most recently.

suggestedApps.disclosure: Shown just above the download button, whose label varies (Install, Start free trial). {host} is a web address like updates.preenwildlife.com.

cull.modes: Preen, a separate culling app, can show inside Lifer's window or run in its own window.
cull.priceUsd: Follows the trial line, so it starts with Then.
cull.counted: Appended to the disclosure sentence. Preen counts trial downloads as a bare total.

suggestedApps.stepVerify: Second of three install steps. Lifer checks the download's signatures before opening it.
suggestedApps.noteWindows: Windows SmartScreen wording: More info and Run anyway are the button names Windows shows.
suggestedApps.licence: A link to the app's licence terms on the publisher's website.
suggestedApps.websiteInstead: A link shown when Lifer can't install the app here or the install failed.

error.notSetUp: Shown when the app's addresses, keys or signer in Lifer are still placeholders.
error.verification: Size, checksum or signature didn't match. Lifer deleted the download.

downloads.back: Back link at the top of Species downloads, a page inside Settings. {group} is that settings group's name, Species and import.
downloads.open: Row at the top of Settings > Species and import that opens Species downloads, where countries and animal groups are downloaded.
downloads.openDescription: Under that row: what a download brings.

account.signIn: Settings group heading for the email and password used to sign in.

ebirdImport.checklists: Shown after an eBird import. {count} is a number of checklists.
ebirdImport.description: <a> wraps a link to eBird's own Download My Data page; keep eBird's page name as eBird shows it in your language. MyEBirdData.csv is a file name, don't translate it.
ebirdImport.summary: After importing an eBird CSV. Each placeholder is a number of species.
ebirdImport.notMatched: <names> wraps a list of species names from the file that matched nothing.

hdrViewer.title: Settings > General > Appearance switch, off by default. HDR (high dynamic range) photos have highlights brighter than normal white; the full-size photo viewer shows them that way when on. Keep HDR as is.
hdrViewer.description: Under Show HDR photos in the viewer. Ultra HDR JPEG is a file format name (a JPEG with extra brightness data); keep it untranslated. Unchanged: thumbnails, grids and screens without HDR keep the standard (SDR) look.

editor.group: Settings > General heading for the photo editor choice (desktop app).
editor.title: Label of the picker of which installed photo editor (Lightroom Classic, darktable...) opens photos.
editor.description: Under Edit photos with. A sidecar is the small .xmp file beside a RAW that holds its edits.
editor.system: Picker option: whatever app the operating system opens photos with.
editor.other: Picker option: opens the system's file picker to choose any other app.

language.automatic: First option of the language picker: use the browser's or operating system's language when Lifer has it, else English.
language.description: Under the Language heading in Settings > General. Species common names are data from the catalog, not part of the interface.

names.title: Section heading in Settings > General: how species cards name each species, and whether they show badges.

packUpdates.description: Species downloads (offline packs) with a newer version on the server.

updates.version: Desktop app version, e.g. "Version 1.2.0." Shown before the update status sentence.
updates.available: {version} is the new version; {current} is the installed version number.
updates.translocated: macOS App Translocation: the app was opened straight from Downloads or a disk image, so it can't update itself.
updates.macGatekeeper: <b> wraps the exact macOS System Settings and button names; use the names macOS shows in your language.
updates.windowsSmartScreen: <b> wraps the exact Windows SmartScreen button names; use the names Windows shows in your language. The quoted text is the warning's title.
updates.windowsInstaller: <a> wraps a link to the GitHub releases page.

map.title: Section heading in Settings > General for the photo map's online options and online place search.
map.mode: Label in Settings > General > Map and places of the Automatic / Off / Satellite choice for the photo map.
map.modeHelp: Under Online map in Settings. {detail} and {imagery} are tile provider names.
map.imageryUrl: Label of a text field in Settings > General > Map and places: an optional satellite tile URL from the user's own provider.
map.imageryUrlHelp: Under the Satellite imagery URL label. Leaving it empty uses the free default imagery.
map.imageryUrlPlaceholder: Placeholder showing the URL shape; {z}, {x} and {y} are passed in as the literal tile placeholders. Keep the URL itself untranslated.
map.imageryUrlInvalid: Error under the Satellite imagery URL field; {z}, {x} and {y} are passed in as the literal placeholders.
map.places: Label in Settings > General > Map and places, and in the map's layers panel: online place search and place names (Automatic or Off).
map.placesHelp: Under Online place names and search in Settings. {provider} is the service name (Photon by komoot).

groups.general: A tab in the Settings sidebar (also listed in the command palette). Keep tab names short.
groups.offlineData: Settings tab for the downloaded species catalog, downloaded regions and maps.

settings.help: Link at the bottom of the Settings sidebar to the online Settings documentation.

integrations.assistantSetUp: Button in Integrations on the desktop app: makes a key and shows the setup to paste into an assistant.
integrations.assistantDescriptionDesktop: Description of the assistant row on the desktop app. Claude Desktop is a product name.
integrations.assistantKeyName: Name given to the key made for an assistant. {date} is today's date.
integrations.assistantKeyFailed: Toast when the key for an assistant couldn't be made.
integrations.assistantModalTitle: Title of the window that shows the assistant setup.
integrations.assistantStep1: Step 1 in the assistant setup window. Claude Desktop is a product name; Settings, Developer and Edit Config are its menu names.
integrations.assistantStep2: Step 2. mcpServers is a name in Claude Desktop's config file and must stay as it is; lifer too.
integrations.assistantStep3: Step 3 in the assistant setup window.
integrations.assistantKeyNote: Note under the setup text: the key can't be shown again. API keys is the name of a Settings page.
integrations.openInat: Button next to Disconnect: opens Lifer's iNaturalist page.
integrations.finishSignIn: Shown after Connect while the person signs in on iNaturalist's site.

folderLayout.example: Before a folder path showing where one of the user's recent photos would be filed with this layout.
folderLayout.sampleExample: Before a folder path showing where a made-up sample photo would be filed, shown before the user has photos.

presets.date: A layout of year then date folders (2025/2025-06-14), the way Lightroom files imports by default.

levels.wildlifeYear: A year folder named like "Wildlife 2025". The folder name itself stays in English on disk.
levels.trip: A folder for the photo's trip, inside a folder named Trips. The folder names stay in English on disk.
levels.group: The animal group folder; the folder names (Birds, Mammals) stay in English on disk.

library.reorganizeResult: Each placeholder is a number of files.

watched.coveredBy: {folder} is a folder path, or the photo library folder, that already includes the one the user chose.

matchingHardware.progress: {step} is the current hardware-test step (an English message from the server); {done} is a formatted download size.
matchingHardware.progressOf: Same, with {total} the full download size.
matchingHardware.busy: {step} is the current hardware-test step, possibly with download progress.
matchingHardware.failed: {message} is the server's English explanation of why the GPU test failed.
matchingHardware.gpu: {device} is the GPU's name, like Apple M2; {ms} is milliseconds per photo; {speedup} is a number like 3.5.

catalog.description: {status} is one of the short status sentences (Up to date., Checking for updates. and so on).
catalog.updatedCount: {species} is a formatted number of species.

offlineData.uses: {size} is a file size like 550 MB.
offlineData.vectorsUpdateFailed: Recognition data: precomputed data the species recognition model compares photos against. {errors} is a list of technical error messages.
offlineData.vectorsDownloadFailed: Recognition data: precomputed data the species recognition model compares photos against. {errors} is a list of technical error messages.

map.description: {status} is the next sentence: Downloaded., About 550 MB., or Uses <size>.

removeConfirm.messageWithSize: {size} is a file size like 550 MB.

model.activeIdentification: BioCLIP 2 is the model's name; keep it.

removeConfirm.messageWithSize: {size} is a file size like 680 MB.

model.sceneMissing: The scene model is the part of species recognition that lets Gallery search match scene and color words.

reimport.title: Settings > Library section for bringing photos already on disk into Lifer.

review.imported: Toast. {species} is the species name the photos were imported as.
review.looksLike: Under an unmatched photo: iNaturalist's confident species suggestion. {species} is a species name.
review.maybe: Under an unmatched photo: iNaturalist's less certain species suggestion. {species} is a species name.
review.matchedMany: {names} is a list of scientific names found in the photo's tags.
review.importAll: Button: import every listed photo with this same suggested species. {count} is how many.

importConfirm.message: {folder} is a folder path. {files} picks whether photos are moved into the library or left in place; {library} adds a sentence when the folder is another Lifer library.

rescanConfirm.messageDrive: {drive} is the name of a registered external drive.

folder.serverRootsHint: LIFER_LIBRARY_ROOTS is an environment variable; keep it as is. Storage is the Settings tab of that name.

rejected.description: Lightroom, Photo Mechanic and digiKam are photo apps; Hidden is a filter name in the Gallery.

import.progress: Job progress detail. RAW files are camera raw image files.

summary.added: After an import. {known} photos were already in the library; {raws} RAW files were matched to photos.
summary.relinked: Files whose drive or folder path changed, so Lifer updated where they are.
summary.missingReferenceData: <a> wraps a link to the downloadable regions that include those species.

unmatched.description: {suggested} is how many of the unmatched photos have an iNaturalist species suggestion.

settings.retry: Button to try loading again after an error.

server.insecureUrl: {urls} is one or more server addresses. Keep http and https:// as is.
server.showingWithExternal: {local} is the home network address; {external} is the address used away from home.
server.remove: Screen reader label of a remove button. {url} is a server address.
server.autoSwitching: Desktop app setting name, kept as a technical term (capitalized as a feature name): switch automatically between a home-network URL and other URLs for the same server.
server.testing: Screen reader label while checking whether an address answers.

naming.commonHint: Example of the common-name format. Use the common name of the American Robin (Turdus migratorius) in your language.
naming.ebirdCodeHint: amerob is the eBird code for American Robin: keep it; translate the rest.
naming.abaCodeHint: AMRO is the ABA code for American Robin: keep it; translate the rest.

species.moveUp: Screen reader label of a reorder arrow. {name} is a name format, like Common name.
species.moveDown: Screen reader label of a reorder arrow. {name} is a name format, like Common name.
species.nameFormatDescription: The user picks and orders name parts (common name, scientific name, codes) used for folder names and photo tags.
species.technicalDiving: Technical diving: deep scuba diving beyond recreational limits, using special gas mixes.
species.hideObscureDescription: Vagrants: species outside their usual range, seen only occasionally. "Seen or photographed" are the two collection states.
species.inatAddDescription: Under the "Add a species from iNaturalist" row: search iNaturalist by name and add the species to a checklist of a region the user picks.

location.saveForLaunchFailed: "Change Server / Library" is the desktop app's menu item; use its translated name. {folder} is a folder path.
location.containerHint: Server (Docker) installs. LIFER_STORAGE_DIR and docker-compose are technical names; keep them as is.

chooseConfirm.title: {folder} is the folder path the user just picked.

drives.namePlaceholder: Example drive name, shown greyed out in the empty field.
drives.lastSeen: When an external drive was last connected. {date} is a formatted date and time.
drives.lastSeenUnknown: Fills {date} in "Last seen {date}" when the date isn't known.

roots.stepMount: Docker setup step. Keep the <code> contents unchanged.
roots.stepSet: Docker setup step. Keep the <code> contents and Label=/container/path unchanged.

removeAll.typeToConfirm: {word} is the English word the user must type (remove); it isn't translated, so keep it as {word}.

health.lastChecked: {when} is a relative time in the interface language, like "3 days ago" or "yesterday".
health.allOk: {when} is a relative time, like "3 days ago"; {count} is how many files were checked.

sync.linkedDescription: {server} is the linked server's address, or "Your server" when it isn't known.

medium.description: Previews are smaller copies of each photo kept on this computer: thumbnails are tiny, medium previews are 1,024 pixels wide.

sync.waiting: {count} is the number of changes made on this computer that the linked server doesn't have yet.
sync.lastSent: {date} is a formatted date and time; the rest are counts of photos uploaded, updated and failed in the last send.
sync.lastCopied: {date} is a formatted date and time; the rest are counts of what the last copy of the server's collection brought here.
sync.libraryLastSent: {date} is a formatted date and time; {count} is how many albums, trips and album photos were sent.

reason.failed: {error} is the server's or the app's English explanation of why the last send stopped.

regions.more: Heading over the offline map and missing reference photo downloads, under the region download picker.

versions.found: After looking for versions in one folder: {linked} files grouped as versions, {suggested} offered for the user to confirm on the Import page.
versions.review: Link under the result of looking for versions; opens the Import page, where possible versions are reviewed.

applyConfirm.message: Confirmation before writing to photos. {updated} is how many photos would change; {edited} is how many have a field the user edited in another app and keep it.

credits.applyKeptEdits: Shown after applying. {count} is how many photos kept a value someone edited in another app.

templates.title: Settings group heading for the templates Lifer writes into each photo's Title, Headline, Description and extra Keywords.

fields.title: Label of the photo Title field (the title other apps show).
fields.headline: Label of the Headline field, a short summary line in the photo's metadata.
fields.caption: Label of the Description field, also called the caption.
fields.keywords: Label of the field for extra keywords written beside the species keywords.

hints.title: One-line description under the Title field label.
hints.headline: One-line description under the Headline field label.
hints.caption: One-line description under the Description field label.
hints.keywords: One-line description under the Extra keywords field label.

placeholders.title: Placeholder inside the empty Title template box.
placeholders.headline: Placeholder inside the empty Headline template box.
placeholders.caption: Placeholder inside the empty Description template box.
placeholders.keywords: Placeholder inside the empty Extra keywords box. Keywords are separated by commas.

fillEmpty.label: Option in a menu choosing how a field is written. Writes only if the file's field is empty.
fillEmpty.hint: Explains the Fill if empty option.

replace.label: Option in a menu choosing how a field is written. Lifer overwrites only text it wrote itself earlier.
replace.hint: Explains the Replace what Lifer wrote option.

append.label: Option in a menu choosing how a field is written. Lifer adds its text after the existing text.
append.hint: Explains the Add to the end option.

off.label: Option in a menu choosing how a field is written. Lifer does not write the field.

templates.ruleLabel: Screen reader name of the write rule menu. {field} is the field name, such as Title.

presets.label: Button opening a menu of ready-made caption templates.
presets.place: Name of a caption preset that lists species, scientific name, place, region and date.
presets.imageOf: Name of a caption preset that reads like 'An image of an Osprey taken on 3 May 2026 with a 500mm f/7.1'.

help.chips: Help text for the template boxes. {brace} is the opening curly brace character that starts a token; keep the placeholder. Tokens show as small chips.
help.optional: Help text about optional wording. {example} is a sample template shown literally, such as [[ taken on {longdate}]]; keep it as is, including the double square brackets.

multi.label: Switch label. On means every species in a photo is named; off means only the main species.
multi.allHint: Description shown while the switch is on.
multi.mainHint: Description shown while the switch is off.

preview.label: Heading of the live preview showing every field for one photo.
preview.sample: Shown when the library has no photos and a made-up photo is used.
preview.photo: {name} is the camera file name of the photo used for the preview, such as IMG_4411.
preview.another: Button that previews the templates on a different photo from the library.
preview.off: Preview text for a field whose write rule is Don't write.
preview.empty: Preview text for a field that would write nothing for this photo.

templates.saveFailed: Error when saving the templates fails.
templates.anotherFailed: Error when loading a different preview photo fails.
templates.dryRunFailed: Error when counting which photos would change fails.
templates.applyNothing: Message when applying would change no photo.

tokenGroups.taxonomy: Group heading in the token menu for scientific classification tokens.
tokenGroups.place: Group heading in the token menu for place and trip tokens.
tokenGroups.capture: Group heading in the token menu for tokens about how and when the photo was taken.
tokenGroups.aggregate: Group heading in the token menu for tokens that cover every species in a photo.

tokens.species: Token menu item and chip: the common name of the species.
tokens.scientific: Token menu item and chip: the scientific (Latin) name.
tokens.group: Token menu item and chip: the broad group such as Birds or Mammals.
tokens.genus: Token menu item and chip: the taxonomic genus.
tokens.family: Token menu item and chip: the taxonomic family.
tokens.order: Token menu item and chip: the taxonomic order.
tokens.class: Token menu item and chip: the taxonomic class.
tokens.place: Token menu item and chip: the place name where the photo was taken.
tokens.region: Token menu item and chip: province or state.
tokens.country: Token menu item and chip: the country.
tokens.trip: Token menu item and chip: the name of the trip.
tokens.date: Token menu item and chip: the date taken, like 2026-05-03.
tokens.longdate: Token menu item and chip: the date taken written out, like 3 May 2026.
tokens.year: Token menu item and chip: the year taken.
tokens.month: Token menu item and chip: the month taken as a number.
tokens.camera: Token menu item and chip: the camera model.
tokens.lens: Token menu item and chip: the lens name.
tokens.focal: Token menu item and chip: the focal length, like 500mm.
tokens.aperture: Token menu item and chip: the aperture, like f/7.1.
tokens.shutter: Token menu item and chip: the shutter speed, like 1/2000s.
tokens.iso: Token menu item and chip: the ISO sensitivity.
tokens.rating: Token menu item and chip: the star rating.
tokens.names: Token menu item and chip: the names of every species in the photo.
tokens.count: Token menu item and chip: how many species the photo shows.

share.notFound: Public page for an album someone shared by link.
share.labels: Checkbox on a shared album: show species names under the photos.

suggestion.match: Under a suggested species card. {percent} is a formatted percentage like 87%: how closely the photo matches the species.

notes.credit: Credit line under text taken from Wikipedia. <article> wraps a link to the article, <licence> a link to the CC BY-SA licence.
notes.sourceCredit: Credit line under a species summary written from another source. {source} is the source's own credit (kept untranslated) in <page>, a link to its page; {licence} is the licence name, in <licence>, a link to it.

species.about: Heading of the collapsible overview card on a species page.

checklists.sea: After the name of an ocean area the user added a species to, to mark it as a sea zone rather than a land region.
checklists.alsoListed: After a checklist the user added a species to, when the built-in catalog already lists the species there.
checklists.removeFrom: {checklist} is a region or ocean area name.
checklists.pickHint: {species} is the species name. "Added by you" is the label shown on species the user added; keep it the same as that label.
checklists.addTo: Button. {name} is the picked region or ocean area.
checklists.noChecklist: {region} is a region name (like a continent) that has no species checklist of its own.

detail.firstObserved: Under the species name. {date} is the date of the user's first photo of it.
detail.seen: Toggle button on a species page: the user has seen this species but not photographed it.
detail.target: Toggle button on a species page: mark the species as one to look for (a target).
detail.dontCount: Menu item: leave this species out of the user's counts (life list totals).
detail.rawGallery: Heading over RAW files of this species that have no matching edited photo.
detail.upload: Title of the upload dialog on a species page.

encounters.encounters: Counts on a species page; <n> wraps the number (shown bold). An encounter is one sighting, however many photos it produced.
encounters.rowPhotos: Right side of a row in the list that opens from the camera, lens or location count: how many of this species' photos used it.
encounters.more: Last row of that list when it is cut short: {count} is how many more cameras, lenses or places there are.

links.inaturalist: Link to the species on iNaturalist (opens in a new tab). Keep the site's name.
links.ebird: Link to the species on eBird (opens in a new tab). Keep the site's name.

photoGrid.filterEdited: Filter on a species page's photos: edited photos (JPEG/HEIC etc.), with how many there are.
photoGrid.bestShot: Badge on the featured photo of a species.
photoGrid.unavailableConnect: Hover text on a dot marking a photo whose original is on a disconnected drive. {volume} is the drive's name.
photoGrid.unavailableNotResponding: Hover text on a dot marking a photo whose original is on a network share (NAS) that is mounted but stopped answering.
photoGrid.fromTrip: Heading of the section of a species page listing photos taken on one trip, shown when the page was opened from that trip. {trip} is the trip's name.
photoGrid.otherPhotos: Heading of the section after the trip's photos on a species page: the species' photos from anywhere else.

photos.placeInRegion: Where a photo was taken. {place} is the place name the user typed (like Prince George), {region} the province, state or country it is in.
photos.yourPhotos: Heading of the user's own photos section on a species page.

picker.listLabel: Accessible name of the species search results list.
picker.searchInaturalistNoMatch: Last row of the species search results. {query} is what the user typed. The arrow means it opens a search on the iNaturalist website.

seasonality.weekRecords: Hover label on a weekly observation bar. {week} is the ISO week number (1 to 52); records are wildlife observation records.
seasonality.weekRecordsIn: Same, scoped to a region. {region} is a region name.

selection.correctIdTo: Select mode, before a species search: move the selected photos to the species picked.
selection.typeSpecies: Placeholder of the species search in select mode: moves the selected photos to the species picked.
selection.hide: Button in select mode: hide the selected photos.

shotData.aperture: Photographic aperture (f-number), e.g. f/5.6. Usually left as is.
shotData.focalLength: Lens focal length in a compact camera-settings line under a photo, e.g. 400mm.

status.localTier: Status tag on a species page: its rarity tier in the region being viewed. {tier} is a tier name such as Rare.
status.vagrant: Status tag: the species turns up here only as a vagrant (a stray outside its normal range).
status.introduced: Status tag: the species is non-native (introduced by people) in this region.
status.endemic: Status tag. {country} is the only country the species is found in.
status.iucn: Status tag. {category} is an IUCN Red List category name, like Least Concern.

speciesCard.tierHere: Small line under a species card's names when the species is rarer in the picked region than worldwide: {tier} is the rarity name, like Rare, giving Rare here.
speciesCard.tierWorldwide: Small line under a species card's names when a region is picked but the species has only a worldwide rarity: {tier} is the rarity name, like Common, giving Common worldwide.

badge.rediscovered: Badge on a species card: the user photographed a species that had been rarely recorded or unrecorded for 25 years.
badge.ghost: Badge on a species card: a species with very few records anywhere.
badge.vagrant: Badge on a species card. A vagrant is a bird or animal far outside its usual range (a birding term).
badge.addedByYouTitle: {list} is a species list name, e.g. "British Columbia's species list".

speciesCard.removedFromList: {name} is a species name, {list} a species list name, e.g. "British Columbia's species list".
speciesCard.archivedToast: {name} is a species name. The species is left out of the user's counts.
speciesCard.addedToTargets: Targets: species the user wants to photograph next.
speciesCard.seenTitle: Hover text on an eye icon: the user saw this species but has no photo of it.
speciesCard.volumeTitle: {drive} is the name of an external drive.

menu.adjustPreview: Menu item: choose how the species card crops its photo.
menu.rarityYours: Menu item. {tier} is a rarity name; (yours) means the user set it themselves.
menu.archiveTitle: "Archived species" is the name of a Settings page; keep it as translated there.

hidePicker.note: Modal with a checkbox for the province and one for its country: hide the species from the checked lists only.

speciesGrid.archiveGroup: Small button after a group heading: leave every species in the group out of the user's counts. Keep it short.

pinned.photographed: Heading of a group pinned above the others: species the user has photographed.
pinned.targets: Heading of a pinned group: species the user wants to photograph next.

speciesGrid.groupProgress: Spoken name of the progress bar under an animal group's heading. {group} is a group name such as Owls or Frogs & Toads.

timeline.title: Stats chart: how many photos were taken each month or year, each bar split by animal group.
timeline.groupBy: Accessible name of the switch between one bar per month and one per year.
timeline.months: Switch option: one bar per month. Also the column heading of the chart's table.
timeline.years: Switch option: one bar per year. Also the column heading of the chart's table.
timeline.herps: Animal group in the chart's legend: reptiles, turtles and amphibians together.
timeline.sea: Animal group in the chart's legend: fish, sharks, rays and other sea creatures such as corals and crabs.
timeline.total: All animal groups together, in the chart's hover card and table.
timeline.range: The dates picked on the chart. {from} and {to} are a month and year, like Mar 2019, or a year.
timeline.rangeStart: Accessible name of the left handle of the date strip under the chart; dragging it changes the first month or year counted.
timeline.rangeEnd: Accessible name of the right handle of the date strip under the chart; dragging it changes the last month or year counted.
timeline.onlyPeriod: Under the chart when every dated photo is from one month or year. {period} is that month and year, like Sep 2026, or a year.
timeline.allDates: Button: stop narrowing the Stats page to the dates picked on the chart.
timeline.showOnMap: Button: open the photo map with only the photos taken in the dates picked on the chart.
timeline.undated: Under the chart: photos it can't place because they have no capture date. {formatted} is {count} with digit grouping.
timeline.emptyRange: Shown instead of the stats when the dates picked on the chart hold no photos.

filter.all: Option of the Stats page's photo filter. Keepers: the edited photos kept in the library.
filter.featured: Option of the Stats page's photo filter: only each species' featured photo.

collection.oneAndDone: Stats card: species with exactly one photo.
collection.ratedOneStar: Beside a species with a single photo rated one star (★).
collection.archiveHealth: Stats card about the library's metadata, such as photos missing a capture date.
collection.ofTotal: After "N photos missing a date": out of how many photos. {total} is the library's photo count.
collection.medianShutter: {shutter} is an exposure time such as 1/500s.
collection.vs: Between two year pickers: compare the first year with the second.

charts.keeperInfo: Info tip on the Stats charts. A keeper is a photo the user kept in their library.
charts.namesAndMore: On a scatter chart dot that stands for several photos. {names} is two species names joined by a comma.
charts.notAvailable: Shown instead of a camera setting (like shutter speed) a photo has no value for.
charts.viewAll: Button under a few thumbnails: opens every photo in the group. The card's heading already gives the count.
charts.body: Filter label: the camera body (as opposed to the lens).
charts.species: Hover label on a chart bar, before a number of species.
charts.setTitle: Title over every photo behind a chart dot or bar. {formatted} is the count with digit grouping; {settings} the camera settings, such as 400mm, 1/1250.
charts.countryPhotos: How many of the user's photos were taken in a country, shown after the country name.
charts.photographedIn: Followed by a short list of country names.

highlights.ofKeepers: Under a stat card. {percent} is a whole number. Keepers: the photos the user kept in their library.
highlights.focalLengthSub: Under the favorite focal length (like 400-600mm): it's the range used most often.
highlights.lifers: Under the best month. A lifer is a species photographed for the first time ever.

stats.noValue: Placeholder in a stats table when there is no value (not applicable).

options.axisOption: Option of the scatter plot's axis pickers, e.g. "X: Focal length". {axis} is X or Y, {field} an EXIF field name.

tierDetails.here: Row label: the species' rarity in the region being browsed.
tierDetails.iucn: Row label: the species' IUCN Red List category.
tierDetails.lifersRarity: First option of the rarity picker: no override, use the rarity Lifer computed.
tierDetails.everywhereNotJust: Checkbox: apply the user's rarity in every region. {place} is the region being browsed.
tierDetails.tierIn: Short fact, e.g. "Occasional in British Columbia". {tier} is a rarity name, {place} a region. Joined to other facts by middle dots.
tierDetails.rareVisitor: Short lowercase fact joined by middle dots: the species is a vagrant here.
tierDetails.easiestIn: Short lowercase fact joined by middle dots. {place} is a country.

why.whereIn: Appended to other lines with its leading space. {place} is a region name.
why.whereWorldwide: Appended to other lines with its leading space, in place of a region.
why.easiestInWhere: {place} is a country; {tier} a lowercase rarity name, like common or rare.
why.inatShare: {share} is a percentage, like 12% or under 0.01%. {group} picks the animal group noun.
why.sightingsShare: {share} is a percentage, like 12% or under 0.01%. {group} picks the animal group noun.
why.seasonLine: {season} is a season phrase like "Mostly Apr to Sep"; the period ends the sentence.

targetLists.addAction: Opens the Add targets dialog, from the Collection's Add species menu and from Settings.
targetLists.tabGroup: Tab: type a group and a place, like raptors of BC, and make every species in it a target.
targetLists.tabImport: Tab: import a CSV file of species names as targets.

group.placeholder: Example phrases in the empty box. BC is British Columbia; keep the examples to well-known groups and places in your language.
group.count: Live preview: how many species would become targets (ones not photographed yet).
group.countAll: Live preview with Include species I've already photographed switched on.
group.inatCount: Live preview for a group only iNaturalist has (plants, insects, fungi): species are added in the background and each becomes a target when it arrives.
group.none: {region} is a region name, like British Columbia.
group.notInCatalog: {query} is what the user typed. Settings and Species and import name a Settings page; keep them as the app's own names.
group.newListNamed: First option of the Add to dropdown: a new target list named after what the user typed. {name} is that text, like raptors of BC.
group.adding: Toast after targeting a group from iNaturalist. {name} is the new list's name, like Mushrooms of British Columbia.

import.done: Toast after importing a target list from a CSV, or targeting a group. {name} is the list's name, which the user typed.
import.notFound: {names} is a comma-separated list of species names from the user's file that matched nothing.
import.offChecklist: Checkbox in the import review. {region} is a region name, like British Columbia.
import.summary: {matched} is a formatted number of names matched to one species; the other parts only show when not zero.

targetLists.nameWithRegion: A target list in a dropdown: its name, then the region it is for in parentheses.
targetLists.summaryGeneral: Under a target list's name in Settings. {count} is a formatted number; the list is not for any one region.
targetLists.summaryRegion: Under a target list's name in Settings. {count} is a formatted number; {region} a region name.

trash.daysLeft: Under a photo in Trash: days until it is permanently deleted.

filter.edited: Filter option: photos whose original is an edited JPEG (not a RAW or video).
filter.raw: Filter option: photos whose only original is a RAW file.

trash.retention: {days} is a number of days, usually 7 or more.

files.summary: Toast when moving a trip's files ends. Skipped files were left where they are (not Lifer's to move); missing ones couldn't be found.
files.linked: Linked: Lifer points at the user's own file where it is, instead of keeping its own copy. "below" is the tickbox "Also move my own linked files".
files.copySpace: {size} is how much space the copies need, like "1.2 GB".

phase.moving: Progress label; {trip} is the trip's name.

card.processing: Screen reader label of the spinner on a trip card while a scan or import runs.
card.counts: Under a trip card. {species} is how many species, {photos} how many photos.

create.namePlaceholder: Hint in the empty trip name field.
create.untitled: Default trip name when none is typed; also used as a folder name.

detail.addMorePhotos: Button that rescans the trip's folder for photos not imported yet.

build.scanInstead: "Add more photos" is the label of the button above; keep it matching that translation.

detail.noPhotosMatch: {search} is the text typed in the search box.
detail.noSpeciesMatch: {search} is the text typed in the search box.

header.tripFolder: Before the path of the folder on disk the trip's photos were imported from.
header.relocate: Link button next to the trip folder's path: choose a different folder for Lifer to look in for new photos.
header.savedTo: Before the path of the folder imported wildlife photos are copied into.
header.species: Trip summary; <n> wraps the number (shown bold).
header.lifers: Trip summary; <n> wraps the number (shown bold). A lifer is a species photographed for the first time ever.
header.rare: Trip summary: how many species of the rare or legendary rarity tier.
header.endemic: Trip summary: how many species found only in one country.

info.addMore: "Add more photos" is the label of a button on the trip page; keep it matching that translation.
info.copiedOnImport: "Save wildlife to" is the label of a field on this page; "Wildlife" is the actual default folder name on disk and should stay as is. RAW is a camera raw file.
info.relocate: "Move trip files to" and "Point to where I moved them" are labels of menu items on the trip page; keep them matching those translations.

jobs.readingCullMarks: Progress step: reading the reject/pick marks a culling app (like Photo Mechanic or SuperPicky) wrote on the photos.
jobs.cullSkipped: After a trip import: photos marked rejected in a culling app were not imported.
jobs.recovered: After a folder scan: photos whose originals had gone missing were found again.
jobs.relinked: After a folder scan: photos whose files had moved inside the folder were linked to the new paths.
jobs.markedStale: After a folder scan: {count} photos whose files are gone; they stay in the library, flagged as stale.

list.importTrip: Button: point Lifer at an existing trip folder on disk.
list.startTrip: Button: create a trip now, before taking or importing its photos.

photoMenu.isCover: Photo menu item when this photo is the trip's cover; choosing it stops using it as the cover.
photoMenu.coverQuad: Cover style option: four photos in a 2 by 2 grid.
photoMenu.adjustPosition: Menu item: adjust how the cover photo is cropped.

scanReview.summary: Above the list of photos a trip folder scan found. {ready} is how many already have a species picked.
scanReview.notWildlife: Joined after the summary with a middle dot: photos that look like no wildlife, so they aren't offered for import.
scanReview.assignSelected: Before a species search: give every selected photo that species.
scanReview.copiedTo: {folder} is a folder path on disk.

start.libraryFolder: Shown as the trip folder's location. Trips/{name} is a folder path inside the user's photo library, keep it as is.

active.badge: Short label on a trip that's going on now; new imports default to it.
active.end: Button: the trip is over, its end date becomes today.
active.markInactive: Button: stop treating this trip as current, whatever its dates.
active.markActive: Button: treat this trip as current, whatever its dates.

dates.since: A trip with no end date yet. {date} is its formatted start date.

checklists.clock: Label of a menu: how far the camera's clock was from the local time at the place.
checklists.clockBehind: Menu option: the camera's clock showed an earlier time than the place. {hours} is a whole number of hours.
checklists.clockAhead: Menu option: the camera's clock showed a later time than the place. {hours} is a whole number of hours.
checklists.matched: Toast after matching photos to eBird checklists. {count} is a number of photos.
checklists.species: {count} is the number of species on an eBird checklist.
checklists.confirm: Button that links the suggested photos to the eBird checklist. {count} is a number of photos.
checklists.gathered: Toast after copying a checklist's photos to a folder. {count} is a number of photos.

suggestions.note: On a trip's page. {name} is the trip, {dates} its formatted date range like May 3 – 10, 2026.
suggestions.add: {count} is how many selected photos join the trip.
suggestions.dismiss: {count} is how many selected photos stop being suggested for this trip.

ui.select: Button that turns on multi-select mode in a photo or species grid.

toast.region: Screen reader name of the area where notification toasts pop up.

job.ofTotal: Progress of a background job, e.g. "12 MB of 40 MB" or "4 of 11". {done} and {total} are already formatted.

ui.selectAll: Selection bar: selects every item in the list, including ones not loaded yet.

selection.selected: Selection bar count of chosen items.

templateField.chip: Screen reader name of a token chip in a template. {name} is the token's name, such as Common name.
templateField.insert: Button opening the menu of tokens to insert into a template.
templateField.insertHint: Tooltip for the Insert button. {brace} is the opening curly brace character; keep the placeholder.

banner.keepDrive: Shown while uploads are being saved to an external drive.
banner.uploading: Status pill shown on every page while uploads run in the background. {done} of {total} files finished; the bracketed parts appear only when some files failed or were skipped as duplicates.
banner.waiting: Status pill shown while uploads pause because the server asked them to slow down (rate limit). They carry on by themselves.

duplicate.message: {fileName} is the uploaded file's name, {species} a species name.
duplicate.messageWithDate: {fileName} is the uploaded file's name, {species} a species name, {date} the date the existing photo was taken.
duplicate.position: After the dialog title when several possible duplicates wait: this is the first of {total}.
duplicate.skip: Button: don't import this file because it is probably a duplicate.
duplicate.skipAll: Possible duplicate dialog, left of the footer: skips every waiting duplicate. {count} is how many are waiting.

raw.addedToFolder: Lower-case status after a RAW file's name. {name} is a species name; each species has a folder for RAW files.
raw.collision: Lower-case status after a RAW file's name. The camera fingerprint is the camera serial plus capture timestamp from EXIF.
raw.descriptionSpecies: On a species page. RAW: a camera's unprocessed image file (CR3, NEF, ARW...). JPEG: the processed photo.
raw.duplicate: Lower-case status after a RAW file's name.
raw.filedUnder: Lower-case status after a RAW file's name. {name} is a species name.
raw.noMatch: Lower-case status after a RAW file's name: no photo in the library matched it, so it was not copied and stays in its folder.

volumeDestination.disconnected: {drive} is the name of an external drive registered in Lifer.
volumeDestination.defaultDrive: Drive picker option. {drive} is an external drive's name.

compare.keep: Screen-reader name of one of two stacked photos on a phone; tapping it keeps that photo. {position} is top or bottom.
compare.pickPrompt: Above two stacked photos on a phone. {step} of {total} counts the comparisons.
compare.label: Screen-reader name of the side-by-side comparison of 2 to 4 photos.

similar.groups: Above the list of groups of near-identical photos (bursts), sorted biggest first.

placeSuggestions.title: Heading over places Lifer suggests naming: spots with photos from several days that no saved place covers. A count follows it.
placeSuggestions.nearTown: Suggested name for a place, from the nearest town in Lifer's offline town list. {town} is that town.
placeSuggestions.unnamed: A suggested place with no town nearby to name it after.
placeSuggestions.photosOnDays: How many photos a suggested place holds and on how many different days they were taken.
placeSuggestions.name: Opens the Add a saved spot dialog, filled in from the suggestion.
placeSuggestions.dismiss: Turns the suggestion down for good; a toast offers Undo.
placeSuggestions.dismissed: Toast after dismissing a suggested place; has an Undo button.
placeSuggestions.dismissFailed: Error when a suggestion couldn't be dismissed.

placePicker.listLabel: Accessible name of the drop-down list of the user's own named places.

group.nearby: Heading in the place list: the user's places closest to the photos.
group.recent: Heading in the place list: places the user filed photos under lately.
group.all: Heading in the place list: every other place, A to Z.

placePicker.metres: A distance under a kilometre, next to a nearby place. {distance} is a formatted number.
placePicker.km: A distance in kilometres, next to a nearby place or as a place's size. {distance} is a formatted number.
placePicker.looksLike: The first row when the photos are inside one of the user's places: offers that place back to them. {name} is the place.
placePicker.addNamed: First row of the place list while the user types a name that isn't one of their places: makes a new place with that name. {name} is what they typed.
placePicker.newPlace: Last row of the place list: makes a new named place by dropping a pin on a map.
placePicker.placeholder: Placeholder of the place picker; the example is a made-up pond name.
placePicker.far: Asked before filing photos under a place they seem far from. {km} is the furthest distance in kilometres.
placePicker.fileAnyway: Files the far photos under the place but keeps their own GPS point.
placePicker.moveToo: Files the far photos under the place and moves their GPS point to the place's centre.

savedSpots.edit: Menu item: edit a saved place's name, size, town, notes and privacy.
savedSpots.editLabel: Accessible name of the inline form editing a place. {name} is the place.
savedSpots.radiusLabel: How big a place is (a radius). Photos inside it count as taken there, and it is sent to iNaturalist as the location's accuracy.
savedSpots.localityLabel: The town and province a place is in, e.g. Prince George, British Columbia, Canada.
savedSpots.localityPlaceholder: Example locality; keep a real town and province.
savedSpots.movePinHere: Link button beside the town or area hint after picking a town from the search: moves the map pin and coordinates to that town's point. Picking a town alone never moves them.
savedSpots.localityAuto: Hint under the town or area field when adding a place and it is empty: Lifer works it out from the place's point.

localitySource.region: Where the town or area text came from: Lifer filled it in from the province.
localitySource.user: Where the town or area text came from: the user typed it.
localitySource.inaturalist: Where the town or area text came from: the user's iNaturalist observations.
localitySource.gazetteer: Where the town or area text came from: the nearest town in Lifer's offline town list.
localitySource.online: Where the town or area text came from: the place the user picked from online search results.
localitySource.townList: Where the town or area text came from: a town or area the user picked from Lifer's offline town list.

savedSpots.workOutAgain: Link under a place's typed town or area: clears it so Lifer fills it in from the nearest town or the province when saved.
savedSpots.notesLabel: Free notes about a place (gate code, best season). Private.
savedSpots.notesHint: Reassures that notes stay on this computer and are never sent anywhere.
savedSpots.alsoRename: Checkbox, ticked by default, when renaming a place: also change the place name on the photos filed under it.
savedSpots.renamedPhotos: Toast after renaming a place also renamed it on its photos; has an Undo button.
savedSpots.nearbyNotIn: Second line of a place in the list: photos taken inside this place that aren't filed under it.
savedSpots.lastUsed: When photos were last filed under this place. {when} is relative, like 3 days ago.

placeSearch.onlineResults: Heading over the place search results found online (after the user's saved spots and regions).
placeSearch.onlineUnavailable: Quiet line under the place search results when the online search failed or is paused; offline results still show.
placeSearch.credit: Credit under online place results. {credit} is the provider and data credit, kept untranslated.
placeSearch.notice: Shown once, under the place search results, the first time an online search is made. Says plainly what is sent and to whom.
placeSearch.gotIt: Dismisses the one-time online place search notice for good.
placeSearch.turnOff: Turns online place search and names off from the one-time notice.

kind.town: Place type after an online result's name: a city, town or village.
kind.park: Place type: a park or nature reserve.
kind.water: Place type: a lake, river or other water.
kind.address: Place type: a street or street address.
kind.region: Place type: a county, province, state or country.

placeSearch.searchingOnline: Quiet line under the place search results while the online search hasn't answered yet (it can be slow on a weak connection). Not an error.

mapRegion.pathLabel: Accessible name of the breadcrumb over the map, like World / Canada / British Columbia.
mapRegion.world: First step of the map breadcrumb: the whole world, zoomed out.
mapRegion.resetView: Button over the map in a country or province: return to that region's designed framing.
mapRegion.resetViewHelp: Tooltip line for Reset view. North up means the map is not rotated or tilted.
mapRegion.alsoIn: Menu button beside the map breadcrumb listing far parts of a region left out of its view, like Svalbard for Norway. {region} is the region's name.
mapRegion.keepZooming: Brief hint over the map while the user zooms out past a framed region's view; zooming out further leaves it for the next level up. {region} is the region's name, like British Columbia.

scope.map: Heading in the keyboard shortcut sheet: keys that work on the map.

action.undoLocation: Keyboard shortcut sheet: Cmd/Ctrl+Z on the map puts back the latest location change.

mapCredits.title: Name and tooltip of the small info button in the bottom-right corner of every map, and the heading of the popover it opens: each map data source's full credit and licence.
mapCredits.alsoUsed: Heading in the map credits popover over sources the map can show but isn't showing now (offline relief, online detail, satellite).

sendPlace.title: Title of the step that files photos under one of the user's named places before sending them to iNaturalist.
sendPlace.titleWithout: Same step, from the Gallery's Send to iNaturalist, when some photos have no location yet.
sendPlace.looksLike: Offered when the photos were taken at or next to one of the user's named places but aren't filed under it. {name} is the place.
sendPlace.useIt: Button after the looks-like line: files the photos under that place.
sendPlace.send: Main button of the place step: files the photos under the chosen place, then sends them to iNaturalist.
sendPlace.setPlace: Button and menu item: file these photos under one of the user's named places (no send).
sendPlace.setPlaceAndSend: Selection bar action on the iNaturalist To send tab: choose a place for the selected sightings, then send them.
sendPlace.sendWithout: Quiet second button: sends to iNaturalist without a location, to be placed on iNaturalist later.
sendPlace.sentObscured: Short line on a sighting: its place's privacy is obscured, so iNaturalist will show only a rough area.
sendPlace.sentPrivate: Short line on a sighting: its place's privacy is private, so iNaturalist will hide the location.
sendPlace.failed: Error under the place step when filing the photos under the place failed.

timeLeft.measuring: Shown under a progress bar until the time left can be measured, like a file copy's first moments.

packProgress.item: {name} is a download, like Canada birds; {current} of {total} counts the downloads in this run.
packProgress.places: {name} is a download, like Canada birds. Shown while its birding spots are added.
packProgress.alsoSettingUp: {name} is a download being set up while another downloads, like Belize birds.

done.downloadMore: Last line of the finish screen. <a> wraps a link to the Species downloads page; keep the path matching the Settings labels.

setup.description: {country} is the first country the user chose, like Canada.

movedPhotos.found: Toast after Lifer updated where moved photos are, with an Undo button.
movedPhotos.undone: Toast after Undo put the photos' old locations back.
movedPhotos.tripFolderMoved: {trip} is a trip name, like Costa Rica 2026; {folder} a full folder path. Shown with Use it and Not now buttons.
movedPhotos.unreadable: Appended to No moved photos found: folders skipped because Lifer isn't allowed to read them.

settings.batch: A row in the list of recent relinks. {date} is a formatted date and time.
settings.batchTrip: A row for a trip whose folder Lifer updated. {trip} is the trip name, {date} a formatted date and time.
settings.placesCount: Heading of the list of folders Lifer searches for moved photos. # is how many folders the user added.
settings.alsoSearched: Under the user's own folders. {list} is a formatted list like "your library folder, 14 trip folders and 2 watched folders", built from libraryFolder, tripFolders and watchedFolders.
settings.libraryFolder: Part of the alsoSearched list, so it starts lower case mid-sentence.
settings.filterLabel: Screen reader label of the filter box above a folder list. {list} is the list's name, like Folders you added.
settings.removeFolder: Screen reader label of the remove (x) button on a folder row. {folder} is the folder's full path.
settings.coveredBy: Shown when the user adds a folder inside one Lifer already searches, so nothing was added. {folder} is the full path of the covering folder.
settings.mergeOffer: Shown after picking a folder that contains folders the user added earlier. Merge replaces them with the new folder.
settings.merged: Toast after merging, with an Undo button.
settings.unmergeFailed: Error toast when Undo of a merge couldn't add any of the old folders back. {folders} is a list of folder names.
settings.unmergePartlyFailed: Error toast when Undo of a merge added only some old folders back. {count} is how many came back; {folders} lists the folder names that didn't.

suggest.line: One-line offer shown where Lifer lists photos it can't find, when they were all in one folder. The button opens a folder picker.
suggest.pickTitle: Title of the folder picker opened from that offer.

versions.badge: A small badge on a photo thumbnail: how many versions (prints, edits, exports) the photo has.
versions.linkToPhoto: Screen reader label of a photo to pick in the link picker. {name} is its file name, like IMG_1234.jpg.
versions.summary: Under the Versions dialog title when the photo has edits, prints or exports filed as versions of it.
versions.filesSummary: Under the Versions dialog title when one photo is held in several files, like a RAW and its JPG. {list} joins the filesRole phrases, like "your camera original and an export".

filesRole.original: One part of the files list: the file straight from the camera.
filesRole.edit: One part of the files list: an edited copy.
filesRole.export: One part of the files list: an exported copy.

versions.oneFile: Under the Versions dialog title when the photo is a single file.
versions.viewFile: Screen reader label of a file's thumbnail in the Versions dialog; opens it full size. {name} is its file name.

label.raw: The automatic name of a version that is only a camera RAW file (CR3, NEF, ARW...), shown beside its JPEG or edit. Usually left as RAW.
label.withSize: A version's name with its print size: {kind} is a version kind like Print, {size} a size like 8x10.
label.numbered: A version's automatic name when two versions of one photo would read the same: {kind} is the name, like Export, {number} counts them from 1.

versions.showingAll: Under the Gallery title when every version is listed as its own photo. {count} is the number of items listed.

notice.found: Shown after Lifer grouped prints, edits and exports of photos. {versions} files were grouped under {photos} photos.

versions.title: Last step of the guided tour, pointing at the Gallery item in the sidebar: photo versions (edits, prints and exports of one photo grouped as one).
versions.body: Tour card text. The stack badge is the small "N versions" label on a photo thumbnail; "Versions" is the item in a photo's ⋯ (more) menu.

lowSpace.message: One line under the toolbar on every page when the disk holding Lifer's data is nearly full. {free} is a size like "4.2 GB".

review.progress: {confirmed} and {total} are counts already formatted with digit grouping, like 2,500.

explorer.resultPath: Under a search result in the Tree of life: {rank} is the group's level (Family) and {path} the groups above it, like Family in Birds / Strigiformes.
explorer.moreResults: Last line of the search results when only the first 50 are listed.
explorer.shape: Screen reader name of the List / Circle switch for the Tree of life.
explorer.circle: Tree of life drawn as rings of groups around a centre (a sunburst chart).
explorer.showGenera: View option: also list the genus level between family and species. Genera is the plural of genus.
explorer.generaHelp: Tooltip on the Show genera option, under the word Genus. Explains the rank to someone who doesn't know it; Icterus is a real Latin genus name, keep it as is.
explorer.allRegions: First link of the Tree of life's region filter: no region, every species in your downloaded regions. Also the button that clears the filter.
explorer.regionPath: Screen reader name of the Tree of life's region trail (All regions › Canada › British Columbia).
explorer.regionEmpty: Tree of life filtered to a region that has no species in your downloaded regions.
explorer.myBranches: Opens the groups you have photographed something in.
explorer.focus: Shows only this group and what is inside it, as if it were the top of the tree.
explorer.zoomOut: Screen reader name of the middle of the circle view; it goes up one group.
explorer.arcLabel: Screen reader name of one ring segment in the circle view, like Owls, 3 of 12 species.
explorer.arcLabelTargets: Screen reader name of a ring segment holding species on your targets, like Owls, 3 of 12 species, 2 targets. Targets are species you want to photograph.
explorer.moreGroups: A ring segment standing in for groups too small to draw separately.
explorer.moreGroupsAction: Screen reader name of the ring segment that stands in for groups too small to draw separately; activating it shows just those groups. Plural forms of: N more groups.
explorer.focusGone: Note above the tree when the group you were looking at is not in the current view (for example after Show only my targets). {group} is the group's name, {shown} the larger group shown instead, or All groups.
explorer.focusGoneRegion: Note above the tree after you pick a region that has none of the group you were looking at. {group} is the group's name, {region} the region, {shown} the larger group shown instead, or All groups.

rank.class: Taxonomic rank, shown small above a group's name.
rank.species: Taxonomic rank, used in search results.

marks.targets: On a group in the Tree of life, and the toolbar link to the Targets list: how many of its species are on your targets (species you want to photograph).
marks.seen: On a group: how many of its species you marked as seen without photographing them.
marks.targetGroup: Button and menu item on a group: adds every species in it you have not photographed to your targets.
marks.seenGroup: Button and menu item on a group: marks every species in it you have not photographed as seen (saw it, no photo).
marks.untargetGroup: Button and menu item on a group: takes every species in it off your targets.
marks.confirmTarget: Confirmation title before targeting a large group. {name} is the group, like Owls.
marks.confirmSeen: Confirmation title before marking a large group as seen. {name} is the group, like Owls.
marks.confirmUntarget: Confirmation title before removing a large group's targets. {name} is the group, like Owls.
marks.doneUntarget: Notice after species were taken off your targets, with an Undo button.
marks.doneUnseen: Notice after a species' seen mark was removed, with an Undo button.
marks.targetsOnly: View option switch: show only the groups and species on your targets.
marks.legend: Legend under the circle view for the small target marker on segments holding species on your targets.
marks.noTargets: Shown when Show only my targets is on and none of your targets are in the region or group shown.
marks.showAll: Button under that message: turns Show only my targets off.

explorer.randomHelp: Tooltip on the Random species button in the Tree of life.
explorer.showMorePhotos: Link under the photo grid of a group in the Tree of life: shows photos of more of its species.

rarity.show: View option switch: add a rarity band to the circle and label rows by rarity tier (common to legendary).
rarity.help: Tooltip on the Show rarity switch. Local rarity is how rare a species is in the picked region.
rarity.group: On a group: {tier} is its average rarity tier name, like Uncommon; {rated} is how many of its species have a tier. Example: Mostly Uncommon, 4 of 20 rare or rarer.
rarity.legend: Screen reader name of the rarity scale under the circle, which lists the tiers from Common to Legendary.
rarity.edge: Lead-in before the rarity scale under the circle: the colours apply to the thin band on each segment's outer edge.
rarity.local: Species detail in the Tree of life: its rarity tier in the picked region, like Legendary in Canada. {tier} is the tier name, {place} the region.
rarity.worldwide: Species detail, under the local rarity when they differ: its rarity tier across its whole range, like Common worldwide.

explorer.shareLegend: Screen reader name of the legend under the circle that explains the green fill.
explorer.legendPhotographed: Legend entry beside a green swatch: the green part of a circle segment is the share of its species you have photographed.
explorer.legendNotYet: Legend entry beside a pale swatch: the empty part of a circle segment is the species you have not photographed yet.

worksWith.title: Settings group heading in Connected apps listing photo apps that read the species keywords Lifer writes into photos.
worksWith.guide: Link button on each row that opens that app's section of the online user guide.
worksWith.guideLabel: Screen reader label for the guide link. {name} is an app name such as Adobe Bridge.

lightroom.name: Product name, do not translate.
lightroom.how: One line under the app name: how to see Lifer's keywords in Adobe Lightroom Classic.

photos.name: Product name, do not translate. Shown on Mac only.
photos.how: One line: how to get Lifer's keywords into Apple Photos. RAW sidecars are separate .xmp files next to a RAW photo.

folders.name: Plain folders of photos, with no catalog app.
folders.how: One line: keywords are stored in the photo files, so any app that reads them works.

bridge.name: Product name, do not translate.
bridge.how: One line: how to see Lifer's nested keyword tree in Adobe Bridge.

photoshop.name: Product name, do not translate.
photoshop.how: One line: where Photoshop shows Lifer's keywords. Camera Raw is Adobe's RAW converter.

dxo.name: Product name, do not translate.
dxo.how: One line: DxO PhotoLab only partly reads Lifer's keywords.

peakto.name: Product name, do not translate.
peakto.how: One line: how to sync Lifer's keywords with Peakto. XMP round trip is the name of a Peakto setting.

fileWriting.title: Settings group heading in Settings > Metadata: where Lifer writes species keywords (inside photo files or in separate .xmp sidecar files).
fileWriting.saveFailed: Error under the group when a setting couldn't be saved.

sidecarNames.label: Row label. A sidecar is a separate small .xmp file next to a RAW photo that holds its keywords.
sidecarNames.description: Row description. IMG_0001.xmp and IMG_0001.CR3.xmp are example file names, do not translate them. App names are product names.
sidecarNames.stem: Dropdown option: an example file name, do not translate.
sidecarNames.full: Dropdown option: an example file name, do not translate.
sidecarNames.both: Dropdown option: write both sidecar file names.

insideFiles.label: Switch label: write keywords into JPEG and similar files themselves.
insideFiles.description: Row description. The format names are file types, do not translate.

help.changes: Info tip paragraph. Checksum is a fingerprint of the file's bytes. Archive health is Lifer's feature that checks files for damage.
help.sidecar: Info tip paragraph explaining what turning the switch off means for other apps.

linked.label: Switch label. Linked folders are folders Lifer reads photos from without copying them into its library.
linked.help: Info tip paragraph: the safety rule for existing sidecar files.
linked.previewFailed: Error when Lifer couldn't count what turning this on would write.

confirm.title: Confirmation dialog title shown before turning the switch on.
confirm.create: List item in the confirmation: how many sidecar files Lifer would create.
confirm.update: List item: how many sidecar files Lifer made earlier would be updated.
confirm.skip: List item: how many sidecar files made by other apps would not be touched.
confirm.unavailable: List item: photos on unplugged drives that would be skipped.
confirm.action: Confirm button: turn the setting on and write the sidecar files.

apply.label: Row label: rewrite photos already in Lifer after changing these settings.
apply.action: Button that starts updating existing photos.
apply.running: Progress label while photos are being updated.
apply.result: Result after the update finished. {count} is a number of photos.
apply.stopped: Result after the user stopped the update. {count} is a number of photos.
apply.failedFiles: Error: how many photos could not be updated. {count} is a number.

applePhotos.action: Menu item for selected photos or an album. Apple Photos is a product name. Shown in the desktop app on Apple computers only.
applePhotos.title: Dialog title.
applePhotos.checking: Progress label while Lifer searches the Apple Photos library for the chosen photos.
applePhotos.sending: Progress label while keywords are added in Apple Photos.
applePhotos.found: Summary before sending. {count} is a number of photos.
applePhotos.notFound: Summary line: photos not in the Apple Photos library are skipped. {count} is a number.
applePhotos.explain: Explains that Lifer only adds keywords and never removes any.
applePhotos.noneFound: Shown when no chosen photo was found in Apple Photos, with how Lifer looks for them.
applePhotos.send: Primary button that adds the keywords.
applePhotos.done: Result after sending. {count} is a number of photos.
applePhotos.unchanged: Result line: photos that already had all the keywords. {count} is a number.
applePhotos.failed: Error line: photos that could not be changed. {count} is a number.
applePhotos.denied: Error when macOS blocked Lifer from controlling Photos. System Settings, Privacy & Security and Automation are names in macOS; use the names macOS uses in your language.
applePhotos.unavailable: Error when the Photos app couldn't be opened.
applePhotos.error: Error for any other failure talking to Apple Photos.
applePhotos.tryAgain: Button that runs the search again.

addOther.title: Dialog title: add species that Lifer has no downloaded list for.
addOther.tabsLabel: Spoken name of the row of tabs at the top of that dialog.
addOther.tabSearch: Tab: find one species by name and put it on the region's checklist.
addOther.tabGroup: Tab: add every species of a group (spiders, butterflies) seen in a place, from iNaturalist. Hidden when the iNaturalist search setting is off.
addOther.tabPaste: Tab: paste species names, one per line, to import them. Hidden when the iNaturalist search setting is off.
